question_data.passage:
In your English class, you are writing an essay on the question, "Should students be allowed to bring smartphones to school?" To prepare, you collected opinions from four classmates and found two sources of information. Read the comments and the sources, and complete your notes.

**Opinions from your classmates**

**Aoi:** I think we should be able to bring our phones. Last winter my train was suddenly stopped because of heavy snow, and I used my phone to tell my parents I would be late. Without it, they would have been worried for hours. Schools should focus on teaching us how to use phones responsibly, not on banning them. After all, we will all use phones every day once we leave school, so learning self-control now is far more useful than simply having the devices taken away from us.

**Ken:** I understand that phones can be handy in an emergency, but in class they are a disaster. Whenever I try to study, a buzzing notification pulls my attention away, and it takes me several minutes to focus again. Honestly, even when my phone is silent in my bag, part of my mind keeps wondering whether a message has arrived. I'd rather leave mine in a locker during lessons. I'm not against phones themselves, only against having them within reach while we are supposed to be learning.

**Mei:** People keep saying phones ruin study, but that's not the whole picture. In our science class we use a dictionary app and look up news articles for discussion, and that has made lessons more interesting. The problem isn't the device; it's the rules. If teachers decide clearly when phones may and may not be used, the same tool that distracts us can actually help us learn. Banning them completely just wastes a chance to teach us a skill we genuinely need.

**Riku:** I worry less about grades and more about how attached we are becoming. Some of my friends check their screens the moment a break starts and barely talk to anyone face to face. If phones are always in our pockets at school, that habit only gets stronger. School should be one place where we step away from our screens and actually practice talking with real people. I'd accept phones being collected each morning and returned at the end of the day.

**Source A**

A recent report from an education research center looked at how mobile phones affect young people's school life. Researchers found that the issue is rarely the phone itself, but how and when it is used. When phones are used under clear teacher guidance—for example, to look up information during a specific task—students often become more engaged. Problems appear when use is unrestricted: students who keep notifications switched on during lessons take noticeably longer to return to a task after each interruption, a delay that adds up across a school day. The report also notes a separate concern: heavy personal phone use during breaks can reduce face-to-face conversation, weakening the social skills that schools are meant to develop. Its overall recommendation is not a total ban but a clear set of rules about when devices may be used.

**Source B**

A survey asked 500 high school students how a change in their school's phone policy affected them. Students whose schools introduced clear rules about when phones could be used were compared with students whose schools simply banned phones completely. The results are shown in the graph below (Source B).

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses Mei's main point?
choices: Whether phones help or harm learning depends on having clear rules for their use.
Smartphones should be banned because they make science lessons too difficult.
Students should be free to use their phones at any time during lessons.
Dictionary apps are the only acceptable use of phones in school.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Whether phones help or harm learning depends on having clear rules for their use.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `depend on ~` のコアは「〜に寄りかかっている」。**結果がそれ次第で変わる**という含み。
- `whether A or B` は「AなのかBなのか」という未決の二択を、名詞のかたまりにする形。
- 「主張の核」を問う設問では、その人が**何を条件として置いているか**を探すのが最短。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mei の結論文:
`[If teachers decide clearly [when phones may and may not be used]], [the same tool [that distracts us]] can actually help us learn.`
  M(条件節)=If teachers decide clearly when phones may and may not be used
  S=the same tool that distracts us / V=can help / O=us / C=learn (原形不定詞)
→ 「**同じ**道具」が条件次第で逆の結果を生む、という構造そのものが
  「whether ... depends on ...」の言い換えになっている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段 Mei。「The problem isn't the device; it's the rules.」でまず対比軸を置き、
続けて「If teachers decide clearly when phones may and may not be used, the same tool that distracts us can actually help us learn.」
と条件を明示する。締めも「Banning them completely just wastes a chance to teach us a skill we genuinely need.」で、
禁止そのものを否定している。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Smartphones should be banned because they make science lessons too difficult.」… Mei は理科の授業で辞書アプリとニュース記事を使い「that has made lessons more interesting」と述べている。難しくなるという記述は本文に無く、評価も逆。
- 「Students should be free to use their phones at any time during lessons.」… Mei が求めるのは「教師が使ってよい時を明確に決める」ことであって、常時自由使用ではない。ルールの必要性を説く主張と正反対。
- 「Dictionary apps are the only acceptable use of phones in school.」… 辞書アプリは例として挙がるだけで、同じ文で news articles も挙げている。「唯一認められる用途」とは述べていない。

questions.stem: What do Ken and Riku have in common in their comments?
choices: Both believe phones should be completely banned from school grounds.
Both think phones bring no benefits to students at all.
Both are willing to accept phones being kept away from students during the school day.
Both are mainly worried about students' grades falling.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Both are willing to accept phones being kept away from students during the school day.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `be willing to V` は「進んで〜する」より「**〜してもかまわない**」という受け入れの姿勢。
- 共通点を問う設問は、**理由が違っても結論が一致していればよい**。動機の一致を探しにいくと外す。
- `would rather V` / `would accept ~ing` はどちらも「その案なら受け入れる」という譲歩の型。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Ken: `[I]'d rather leave [mine] [in a locker] [during lessons].`
  S=I / V=would rather leave / O=mine (= my phone) / M=in a locker, during lessons
Riku: `[I]'d accept [phones being collected each morning and returned at the end of the day].`
  S=I / V=would accept / O=動名詞句 (phones が意味上の主語・being collected と returned が並列)
→ 動詞は違うが、どちらも「日中は手元から離す」案の**受け入れ**を目的語に取っている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段 Ken「I'd rather leave mine in a locker during lessons.」
第4段 Riku「I'd accept phones being collected each morning and returned at the end of the day.」
二人とも授業中・在校中は端末を手元から離すことを容認している。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Both believe phones should be completely banned from school grounds.」… Ken は「I'm not against phones themselves」と明言し、Riku も下校時の返却を前提にしている。校内からの完全排除ではない。
- 「Both think phones bring no benefits to students at all.」… Ken は冒頭で「I understand that phones can be handy in an emergency」と利点を認めている。「利点は一切ない」ではない。
- 「Both are mainly worried about students' grades falling.」… Riku は「I worry less about grades and more about how attached we are becoming」と述べ、成績ではなく依存を問題にしている。

questions.stem: Whose opinion is most clearly in agreement with the recommendation made in Source A?
choices: Aoi, because she says phones must always be available to students.
Ken, because he wants phones locked away at all times.
Riku, because he focuses only on reducing screen attachment.
Mei, because she argues that clear rules let phones help learning.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Mei, because she argues that clear rules let phones help learning.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `not A but B` は「AではなくB」。**主張は必ず but の後**にある。
- 「どの意見が資料の推奨と一致するか」型は、まず資料の**結論文だけ**を取り出してから
  各人の主張と突き合わせる。資料全体の話題(依存・集中)に引きずられないこと。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Source A の結論文:
`[Its overall recommendation] is [not a total ban] but [a clear set of rules [about when devices may be used]].`
  S=Its overall recommendation / V=is / C=not a total ban but a clear set of rules
  M=about when devices may be used (前置詞 + 疑問詞節)
→ C が not A but B。取るべきは B =「いつ使ってよいかの明確なルール」。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「When phones are used under clear teacher guidance—for example, to look up information during a specific task—students often become more engaged.」
で指導下の有効性を示し、末尾で「Its overall recommendation is not a total ban but a clear set of rules about when devices may be used.」と結ぶ。
これは Mei の「教師が使用時を明確に決めれば道具は学習を助ける」と同じ主張。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Aoi, because she says phones must always be available to students.」… Source A は「Problems appear when use is unrestricted」と無制限使用の弊害を述べており、常時利用可という Aoi の立場は推奨と合わない。
- 「Ken, because he wants phones locked away at all times.」… Source A の結論は「not a total ban」。常時締め出しを求める Ken の立場は推奨と逆向き。
- 「Riku, because he focuses only on reducing screen attachment.」… Source A は対面会話の減少にも触れるが、それは「a separate concern」として添えられた論点で、結論はあくまで使用ルールの整備。

questions.stem: What conclusion can be drawn from Source A?
choices: The mere presence of a phone is the main cause of poor learning.
The way and timing of phone use, rather than the phone itself, determines its effect on school life.
Notifications during lessons have no measurable effect on students' focus.
Schools should remove all phones to protect students' social skills.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The way and timing of phone use, rather than the phone itself, determines its effect on school life.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `rarely A, but B` は「めったにAではなく、むしろB」。**頻度の副詞が否定を担う**型。
- `A rather than B` は「BではなくA」で、**前が主役**。not A but B と前後が逆なので注意。
- 資料の結論を問う設問は、本文が繰り返し置いている**対比軸**を見つければ答えが決まる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Researchers] found [that [the issue] is [rarely the phone itself], but [how and when it is used]].`
  S=Researchers / V=found / O=that 節
  that 節内: S=the issue / V=is / C=rarely the phone itself, but how and when it is used
  (C に疑問詞節 how and when ... が入り、「使い方と時機」が補語になっている)
→ 「端末そのもの」対「使い方と時機」という対比が、そのまま設問の答えの軸。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A 冒頭「Researchers found that the issue is rarely the phone itself, but how and when it is used.」
以降も同じ軸で一貫している。指導下では「students often become more engaged」、
無制限使用では「students who keep notifications switched on during lessons take noticeably longer to return to a task after each interruption」。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The mere presence of a phone is the main cause of poor learning.」… 本文は「the issue is rarely the phone itself」と明言している。端末が存在すること自体が主因という読みは正反対。
- 「Notifications during lessons have no measurable effect on students' focus.」… 無制限使用の生徒は復帰に「noticeably longer」かかると、測定できる差として書かれている。影響なしとは述べていない。
- 「Schools should remove all phones to protect students' social skills.」… 結論は「not a total ban」。社会性への懸念は述べるが、全端末の撤去は推奨されていない。

questions.stem: Which statement is best supported by Source B when read together with the opinions and Source A?
choices: Clear-rules schools supported Mei's view by letting far more students use phones for learning, while total bans did better at increasing face-to-face talk, matching Riku's concern.
Clear rules and total bans produced almost the same result for using phones to learn.
Total-ban schools were better than clear-rules schools at helping students use phones for learning.
Because total-ban schools had the highest single figure, banning phones is clearly the best overall policy.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Clear-rules schools supported Mei's view by letting far more students use phones for learning, while total bans did better at increasing face-to-face talk, matching Riku's concern.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 図と複数の意見を突き合わせる設問は、**指標ごとに「誰の主張を裏づけるか」を 1 対 1** で対応させる。
- 指標が複数あるときに、**最大値ひとつで全体を語らない**のが鉄則。
  「最も高い数字が出た方が優れた政策」は典型的な過度の一般化。
- `while` は対比の接続詞。前半と後半で**別々の指標**を語っていることが多い。

## 🔬 文構造分析
正答の選択肢:
`[Clear-rules schools] supported [Mei's view] [by letting far more students use phones for learning], while [total bans] did better [at increasing face-to-face talk], [matching Riku's concern].`
  主節: S=Clear-rules schools / V=supported / O=Mei's view / M=by ~ing (手段)
  対比節: S=total bans / V=did better / M=at ~ing (どの点で優れたか)
  末尾の matching ~ は分詞構文で「それが誰の懸念と合うか」を添える。
→ **2 つの指標を 2 人に振り分ける**構造。片方の指標だけを見る選択肢は落ちる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
図(Source B)より、「Used phone for learning」は Clear-rules 58% に対し Total-ban 14%。
「More face-to-face talk」は Total-ban 71% に対し Clear-rules 49%。
前者は Mei「If teachers decide clearly when phones may and may not be used, the same tool that distracts us can actually help us learn.」を、
後者は Riku「School should be one place where we step away from our screens and actually practice talking with real people.」を裏づける。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Clear rules and total bans produced almost the same result for using phones to learn.」… 学習活用は 58% と 14% で 4 倍以上の開きがある。「ほぼ同じ結果」とは言えない。
- 「Total-ban schools were better than clear-rules schools at helping students use phones for learning.」… 学習活用は Clear-rules 58% > Total-ban 14%。優劣が逆になっている。
- 「Because total-ban schools had the highest single figure, banning phones is clearly the best overall policy.」… 最大値の 71% は Total-ban の対面会話だが、同じ Total-ban は学習活用で 14% と大きく劣る。単一の指標だけで全体を結論づけている。

In your English class, you are writing an essay on the topic "Should high school students reduce their club activity hours to focus more on study?" To prepare, you collected opinions from four classmates and found two sources.

Daichi: I strongly believe clubs should keep their current hours. At my baseball club, I learned how to manage my time far better than I ever did before. Because practice ends late, I have to use the short gaps in my day wisely, and my grades have actually gone up since I joined. Cutting club time would not give students more useful study hours; it would just take away the very place where I learned discipline.

Hana: I see things differently. Many of my friends in the brass band practice until eight at night, then start homework exhausted. They fall asleep in class the next day. I am not against clubs themselves, but the hours have become too long. If schools limited practice to a reasonable level, students could rest properly and still enjoy their activities. Balance is the real goal, not choosing one side over the other.

Riku: For me, the answer depends on the student. A few of my classmates are aiming for very competitive universities, and for them every extra hour matters. But others find their main purpose in club life, and forcing them to study more would only make them unhappy. Schools should not set one rule for everyone. Instead, students themselves should be allowed to decide how much time their clubs take.

Mei: Honestly, I think the worry about clubs is exaggerated. Studies that compare students often forget that active, motivated people tend to do many things well at once. The problem is not the clock but how tired students are. A shorter practice that is poorly organized helps no one, while a long but well-run practice can leave students fresh enough to study. We should focus on the quality of practice, not simply the number of hours.

Source A:
Researchers who study teenagers point out that the link between club hours and school performance is not as simple as it first appears. In several studies, students who spent moderate time in clubs scored higher on tests than students who did no club activity at all, while those with extremely long practice hours scored lower. Experts explain this as a curve rather than a straight line: a reasonable amount of activity supports concentration and motivation, but beyond a certain point, tiredness begins to harm learning. Importantly, the researchers warn that comparing club members and non-members directly can be misleading, because committed students often differ in personality and habits before they ever join a club. The amount of sleep students get, they conclude, may matter more than the raw number of hours spent at practice.

Source B:
A national survey asked first-year high school students how many hours they spent on weekday club practice and recorded their average test scores and average nightly sleep. The results are summarized in the graph below (Source B). Students were grouped by their daily practice length, and for each group the survey reported both the average test score (out of 100) and the average hours of sleep on a school night.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses Daichi's opinion?
choices: Club hours should be reduced so that students can finally get enough sleep at night.
Club activities should keep their hours because they teach skills like time management that actually help studying.
Whether to cut club hours should be left entirely up to each individual student.
The number of practice hours matters less than how well each practice is organized.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Club activities should keep their hours because they teach skills like time management that actually help studying.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 意見の要約を問う設問は、「**結論**＋**その理由**」の両方を含む選択肢を選ぶ。
  結論だけ合っていて理由が別人のもの、という誤答がよく混ざる。
- `keep their hours` = 現状維持。`cut / reduce` = 削減。まずどちら側かを確定する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Because practice ends late], [I] have to use [the short gaps in my day] [wisely], and [my grades] have actually gone up [since I joined].`
  M(理由節)=Because practice ends late
  S=I / V=have to use / O=the short gaps in my day / M=wisely
  等position節: S=my grades / V=have gone up / M=since I joined
→ 「練習が長い」→「隙間時間を使う力がついた」→「成績が上がった」という
  因果の鎖。だから時間を削るなという主張につながる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段 Daichi。「At my baseball club, I learned how to manage my time far better than I ever did before.」
で得たものを述べ、「Cutting club time would not give students more useful study hours; it would just take away the very place where I learned discipline.」
で削減を否定する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Club hours should be reduced so that students can finally get enough sleep at night.」… 時間短縮と睡眠の確保は Hana の主張。Daichi は「clubs should keep their current hours」と現状維持を求めている。
- 「Whether to cut club hours should be left entirely up to each individual student.」… 生徒個人の裁量に委ねるべきというのは Riku の主張。Daichi は全体として現状維持を主張している。
- 「The number of practice hours matters less than how well each practice is organized.」… 練習の質を時間数より重視するのは Mei の主張。Daichi は時間があることで身についたものを語っている。

questions.stem: What do Hana and Mei have in common in their opinions?
choices: Both insist that all schools must set a strict legal limit on club practice hours.
Both conclude that students should personally decide how long their clubs run.
Both think that students' tiredness, rather than the existence of clubs itself, is the key issue.
Both argue that club activities have no real effect on academic performance.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Both think that students' tiredness, rather than the existence of clubs itself, is the key issue.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 共通点を問う設問は、**結論の一致**ではなく「**何を問題の中心に置いているか**」で揃うことがある。
- `A rather than B` = 「BではなくA」。何を主犯と見るかを示す型。
- 「〜そのものには反対しない」という譲歩表現は、**争点をずらす合図**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mei の中心文:
`[The problem] is [not the clock] but [how tired students are].`
  S=The problem / V=is / C=not the clock but how tired students are
  (not A but B の B に疑問詞節 how tired students are が入る)
Hana の中心文:
`[I] am not against [clubs themselves], but [the hours] have become [too long].`
  → どちらも「クラブの存在」を否定せず、争点を**疲労・時間の質**に移している。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段 Hana「I am not against clubs themselves, but the hours have become too long.」
「If schools limited practice to a reasonable level, students could rest properly and still enjoy their activities.」
第4段 Mei「The problem is not the clock but how tired students are.」
二人とも、クラブの存在ではなく生徒の疲労・休息を核心と見ている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Both insist that all schools must set a strict legal limit on club practice hours.」… Hana は「a reasonable level」への制限を望むが法的規制とは述べていない。Mei はむしろ時間で区切る発想そのものを否定している。
- 「Both conclude that students should personally decide how long their clubs run.」… 生徒本人が決めるべきという主張は Riku のもの。Hana は学校による制限、Mei は練習の質を求めている。
- 「Both argue that club activities have no real effect on academic performance.」… Hana は長時間練習の翌日に「They fall asleep in class the next day.」と学業への影響を述べている。影響がないとは考えていない。

questions.stem: Whose opinions are most directly supported by Source A?
choices: Daichi and Riku
Riku and Mei
Daichi and Hana
Hana and Mei
questions.explanation:
正解は「Hana and Mei」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「誰の意見が資料に支持されるか」型は、**資料の論点を先に取り出す**。
  ここでは (1) 適度なら有益・過度は有害 (2) 睡眠が時間数より重要かも
  (3) 部員と非部員の単純比較は危うい、の 3 点。
- 資料が扱っていない論点(現状維持・個人裁量)を語る人は、正しくても「支持される」には当たらない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Source A の結論文:
`[The amount of sleep [students get]], [they conclude], may matter [more than the raw number of hours [spent at practice]].`
  S=The amount of sleep students get / V=may matter / M=more than the raw number of hours spent at practice
  they conclude は挿入節 (主語・動詞を割り込ませる形)
→ 比較の軸が「練習時間」ではなく「睡眠量」に置き換えられている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「a reasonable amount of activity supports concentration and motivation, but beyond a certain point, tiredness begins to harm learning」
と山なりの関係を述べ、末尾で「The amount of sleep students get, they conclude, may matter more than the raw number of hours spent at practice.」と結ぶ。
これは Hana の「students could rest properly」と、Mei の「The problem is not the clock but how tired students are.」に直接対応する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Daichi and Riku」… Daichi は現状維持、Riku は個人裁量で、どちらも Source A が軸に置く疲労・睡眠の議論に触れていない。
- 「Riku and Mei」… Mei は合致するが、Riku の「生徒本人が決めるべき」は Source A が扱っている論点ではない。
- 「Daichi and Hana」… Hana は合致するが、Daichi の「時間管理が身についた」は Source A の疲労・睡眠の議論とは別の話。

questions.stem: What conclusion can be drawn from Source A?
choices: A moderate amount of club activity can help learning, but too much may hurt it mainly because students lose sleep.
The more hours a student practices, the higher that student's test scores will steadily become.
Doing no club activity at all is the surest way to achieve the highest test scores.
Differences in test scores between club members and non-members are caused only by the number of practice hours.
questions.explanation:
正解は「A moderate amount of club activity can help learning, but too much may hurt it mainly because students lose sleep.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `a curve rather than a straight line` = 「**山なり**の関係であって単調増加ではない」。
  曲線と言われたら「途中までは上がる、どこかから下がる」と読む。
- 資料の結論を問う設問では、**両端(ゼロと過剰)がどちらも最良でない**という形の
  選択肢が正解になりやすい。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[students [who spent moderate time in clubs]] scored [higher on tests] than [students [who did no club activity at all]], while [those [with extremely long practice hours]] scored [lower].`
  S=students who spent moderate time in clubs / V=scored / M=higher on tests than ...
  while 節: S=those with extremely long practice hours / V=scored / M=lower
→ 「適度 > ゼロ」かつ「過剰 < 適度」。この 2 つを同時に満たす読みが山なりの関係。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「Experts explain this as a curve rather than a straight line: a reasonable amount of activity supports concentration and motivation, but beyond a certain point, tiredness begins to harm learning.」
さらに「The amount of sleep students get, they conclude, may matter more than the raw number of hours spent at practice.」
と、過剰が害になる経路として睡眠を挙げている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The more hours a student practices, the higher that student's test scores will steadily become.」… 本文は「a curve rather than a straight line」と明言している。練習時間に比例して得点が上がり続けるという読みは、この一文に真っ向から反する。
- 「Doing no club activity at all is the surest way to achieve the highest test scores.」… 適度な活動をした生徒は「students who did no club activity at all」より高得点だと書かれている。活動ゼロが最良という結論は逆。
- 「Differences in test scores between club members and non-members are caused only by the number of practice hours.」… 本文は「comparing club members and non-members directly can be misleading」と警告し、「differ in personality and habits before they ever join a club」と述べている。差の原因を練習時間だけに帰することはできない。

questions.stem: Which statement is best supported by Source B when read together with the opinions and Source A?
choices: Because the 0-hour group does not have the highest score, club activities must always raise test scores no matter how long they last.
The group practicing 4+ hours has both the lowest test score and the least sleep, supporting the view that excessive practice and lost sleep can harm learning.
Since the 2-hour group sleeps fewer hours than the 1-hour group, more sleep always leads directly to higher test scores.
The steady rise in scores from 0 to 4+ hours shows that students should practice as long as possible.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The group practicing 4+ hours has both the lowest test score and the least sleep, supporting the view that excessive practice and lost sleep can harm learning.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 2 系列のグラフは、**両方が同じ向きに振れている群**を探すと資料の主張と結びつく。
- 「最高」「最低」は必ず**数値で確かめる**。印象で決めると、単調増加でないグラフを
  単調と読み違える。
- 分詞構文 `supporting ~` は「その事実が何を裏づけるか」を後ろから添える形。

## 🔬 文構造分析
正答の選択肢:
`[The group [practicing 4+ hours]] has [both the lowest test score and the least sleep], [supporting the view [that excessive practice and lost sleep can harm learning]].`
  S=The group practicing 4+ hours (practicing 以下は現在分詞の後置修飾)
  V=has / O=both A and B (2 つの指標を同時に持つことが要点)
  supporting ~ = 分詞構文。that 節は the view の同格。

## 📍 本文の根拠
図(Source B)より、4+ hrs 群は test score 58 で最低、sleep 5.6 時間で最少。
最高得点は 2 hrs 群の 71 で、0 hrs 群は 62。
これは Source A の「beyond a certain point, tiredness begins to harm learning」と、
Mei の「The problem is not the clock but how tired students are.」を同時に裏づける。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because the 0-hour group does not have the highest score, club activities must always raise test scores no matter how long they last.」… 4+ hrs 群は 58 点で、0 hrs 群の 62 点より低い。「どれだけ長くても常に得点を上げる」は図と矛盾する。
- 「Since the 2-hour group sleeps fewer hours than the 1-hour group, more sleep always leads directly to higher test scores.」… 2 hrs 群は睡眠 7.1 時間で 1 hr 群の 7.5 時間より少ないのに、得点は 71 > 68 と高い。この群自体が「睡眠が多いほど高得点」の反例になっている。
- 「The steady rise in scores from 0 to 4+ hours shows that students should practice as long as possible.」… 得点は 62 → 68 → 71 と上がったあと 66 → 58 と下がる。単調増加ではないので、長いほどよいという結論は導けない。

question_data.passage:
For your English class, you are writing a report on the question, "For studying, are paper books or e-books better?" You have collected opinions from four classmates and two sources of information.

Riku: I strongly prefer paper books for studying. When I read on paper, I can see how far I have come just by feeling the pages, and that sense of progress keeps me going. I also write notes in the margins and underline important points by hand, which helps me remember them later. With a screen, I tend to skim quickly and forget what I read. For me, paper simply makes deep, focused study possible, even if it is heavier to carry around.

Mei: Honestly, I think e-books are the smarter choice for students today. I carry hundreds of textbooks on one light tablet, and I can search for any word in a second instead of flipping through pages. The built-in dictionary saves me so much time when I study English. Of course, screens can tire my eyes, so I take short breaks. But the convenience is worth it. If we want to study anywhere, anytime, e-books are clearly the better tool.

Aoi: I don't think one is simply better than the other; it depends on what you are doing. For quick review or looking things up, e-books are excellent because they are fast and portable. But when I really need to concentrate and understand something difficult, paper helps me stay focused without notifications pulling my attention away. So I use both, choosing the right tool for each task rather than insisting that only one works.

Sota: I used to love new gadgets, but my own experience changed my mind. Last year I switched to studying entirely on a tablet, and my test scores actually dropped. I kept getting distracted by messages and other apps, and I rarely remembered where information appeared. When I went back to paper for my hardest subjects, my concentration returned. I'm not against technology, but for serious studying that demands memory, paper works better for me.

Source A:
Researchers have studied how the reading medium affects learning. Several experiments show that when people read informative texts to understand and remember them, they often perform slightly better on paper than on screens. One reason may be that the physical layout of a page helps readers build a mental "map" of where information is located, which supports memory. Screens, by contrast, often invite faster, shallower reading and carry the risk of digital distractions such as messages or links. However, researchers also note that the device itself is not the only factor. How carefully a student reads, and whether they avoid distractions, can matter just as much as the medium. For tasks like quick searching or skimming, digital texts can even be more efficient.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main point of Aoi's opinion?
choices: Paper books are always better than e-books for any kind of study.
E-books should replace paper books because they are faster and lighter.
Students should avoid screens entirely to protect their concentration.
Neither format is best overall; the right choice depends on the task.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Neither format is best overall; the right choice depends on the task.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `it depends on ~` は「〜次第」。二者択一を問われて「どちらとも言えない」と答える型では、
  必ず**何によって決まるか**という判断基準が示される。そこが主張の核。
- `rather than ~ing` = 「〜するのではなく」。捨てた側を示すので、主張は前半にある。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Aoi の冒頭:
`[I] don't think [one is simply better than the other]; [it] depends on [what you are doing].`
  S=I / V=don't think / O=that 節 (接続詞 that が省略)
  セミコロン以降: S=it / V=depends on / O=what you are doing (疑問詞節)
→ 前半で二者択一そのものを否定し、後半で判断基準を置く。この 2 段構えが
  「Neither ... best overall; the right choice depends on the task.」と同じ形。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段 Aoi。「I don't think one is simply better than the other; it depends on what you are doing.」
と述べたうえで、「So I use both, choosing the right tool for each task rather than insisting that only one works.」
と締める。用途で使い分けるという立場が一貫している。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Paper books are always better than e-books for any kind of study.」… Aoi は「For quick review or looking things up, e-books are excellent」と電子書籍の利点を認めている。always とは言えない。
- 「E-books should replace paper books because they are faster and lighter.」… 電子書籍への全面移行を主張するのは Mei。Aoi は「I use both」と併用を明言している。
- 「Students should avoid screens entirely to protect their concentration.」… Aoi は電子書籍を「excellent」と評価して実際に使っている。画面を完全に避けよとは述べていない。

questions.stem: What do Riku and Sota have in common in their opinions?
choices: Both say that paper helps them concentrate and remember better.
Both believe e-books are better for memorizing difficult material.
Both prefer tablets because they are lighter and easier to carry.
Both think the choice of format makes no real difference to studying.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Both say that paper helps them concentrate and remember better.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 共通点は「**違う道筋から同じ結論**」に至っている場合が多い。
  Riku は好みと習慣から、Sota は失敗経験から、同じ結論に着いている。
- `make O C` = 「O を C の状態にする」。`help + O + 原形` = 「O が〜するのを助ける」。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Riku: `For me, [paper] simply makes [deep, focused study] [possible], even if [it] is [heavier to carry around].`
  S=paper / V=makes / O=deep, focused study / C=possible (make O C)
  even if 節=譲歩。「重くても」と不利を認めたうえで結論を守る形。
Sota: `[When I went back to paper for my hardest subjects], [my concentration] returned.`
  M(時の節)=When I went back to paper for my hardest subjects / S=my concentration / V=returned

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段 Riku「For me, paper simply makes deep, focused study possible, even if it is heavier to carry around.」
「I also write notes in the margins and underline important points by hand, which helps me remember them later.」
第4段 Sota「When I went back to paper for my hardest subjects, my concentration returned.」
画面については「I rarely remembered where information appeared」。集中と記憶の 2 点で一致する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Both believe e-books are better for memorizing difficult material.」… 二人とも逆の立場で、Sota は「for serious studying that demands memory, paper works better for me」と明言している。
- 「Both prefer tablets because they are lighter and easier to carry.」… 軽さ・携帯性を利点に挙げるのは Mei。Riku はむしろ紙が「heavier to carry around」だと認めたうえで紙を選んでいる。
- 「Both think the choice of format makes no real difference to studying.」… Sota は媒体を変えて「my test scores actually dropped」と実際の差を報告している。違いは無いとは考えていない。

questions.stem: Whose opinion is most clearly supported by the information in Source A?
choices: Mei, because Source A says e-books are better for all serious study.
Sota, because Source A links screens to distraction and weaker memory.
Riku, because Source A says handwriting in margins is always necessary.
No one, because Source A states the device makes no difference at all.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Sota, because Source A links screens to distraction and weaker memory.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「誰の意見が資料に支持されるか」型は、資料が示す**因果の向き**を確かめる。
  ここでは「画面 → 速く浅い読み・注意散漫 → 記憶が弱い」。
- 選択肢は「誰」＋「because 以下の理由」の 2 つでできている。
  **人が合っていても理由が資料と違えば誤り**なので、後半まで必ず読む。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Screens], by contrast, often invite [faster, shallower reading] and carry [the risk of digital distractions [such as messages or links]].`
  S=Screens / V=invite ... and carry ... (等位の 2 動詞) / M=by contrast, often
  O1=faster, shallower reading / O2=the risk of digital distractions such as messages or links
→ 1 つの主語に 2 つの述語がぶら下がり、「浅い読み」と「気の散り」を同時に述べる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「One reason may be that the physical layout of a page helps readers build a mental "map" of where information is located, which supports memory.」
で紙が記憶を支える理屈を示し、対比として「Screens, by contrast, often invite faster, shallower reading and carry the risk of digital distractions such as messages or links.」
と述べる。これは Sota の「I kept getting distracted by messages and other apps, and I rarely remembered where information appeared.」に正確に対応する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Mei, because Source A says e-books are better for all serious study.」… Source A は「they often perform slightly better on paper than on screens」と紙がやや有利と述べており、電子が全面的に優れるとは書いていない。
- 「Riku, because Source A says handwriting in margins is always necessary.」… Source A に余白への手書きについての記述は無い。Riku 自身の習慣であって資料の裏づけではない。
- 「No one, because Source A states the device makes no difference at all.」… Source A は「the device itself is not the only factor」と述べている。「唯一の要因ではない」であって「差が無い」ではない。

questions.stem: Which conclusion can best be drawn from Source A?
choices: The reading device alone decides how well a student learns.
Screens are useless for any kind of academic study.
The medium matters, but how carefully a student reads matters too.
Paper is more efficient than screens for every reading task.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The medium matters, but how carefully a student reads matters too.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `not the only factor` は「**他にもある**」であって「関係ない」ではない。
  限定の否定を全否定と読み違えるのが典型的な失点。
- `just as much as ~` = 「〜と同じくらい」。両者を並べて**どちらも重い**と言う型。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[How carefully a student reads], and [whether they avoid distractions], can matter [just as much as the medium].`
  S=How carefully a student reads / whether they avoid distractions (疑問詞節と whether 節が並列して主語)
  V=can matter / M=just as much as the medium
→ 主語が「読み方」と「気を散らさないか」の 2 つ。媒体と同格に置かれている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「However, researchers also note that the device itself is not the only factor.」に続けて
「How carefully a student reads, and whether they avoid distractions, can matter just as much as the medium.」
と述べ、さらに「For tasks like quick searching or skimming, digital texts can even be more efficient.」と補う。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The reading device alone decides how well a student learns.」… 「the device itself is not the only factor」と正面から矛盾する。媒体だけで決まるとは書かれていない。
- 「Screens are useless for any kind of academic study.」… 「For tasks like quick searching or skimming, digital texts can even be more efficient.」と矛盾する。用途によっては電子が有利。
- 「Paper is more efficient than screens for every reading task.」… 同じ一文で検索・流し読みでは電子が効率的だと述べており、every task で紙が優るとは言えない。

questions.stem: Based on Source B, which statement is best supported when read together with the classmates' opinions and Source A?
choices: Because most students chose e-books for carrying many books, e-books must also be better for deep reading.
Since 72% preferred paper for deep reading, no student finds e-books useful for any purpose.
The survey shows students favor paper for tasks needing concentration and memory, but e-books for searching and portability, matching the idea that each format suits different tasks.
The high e-book figure for quick search proves that paper books make searching impossible.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The survey shows students favor paper for tasks needing concentration and memory, but e-books for searching and portability, matching the idea that each format suits different tasks.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- グラフと意見を突き合わせる設問では、**課題の種類ごとにどちらが選ばれたか**を並べてから、
  その並び全体と一致する主張を探す。
- 1 つの課題の数値から**別の課題へ結論を広げない**。これが最も多い誤答の型。

## 🔬 文構造分析
正答の選択肢:
`[The survey] shows [students favor paper for tasks [needing concentration and memory], but e-books for searching and portability], [matching the idea [that each format suits different tasks]].`
  S=The survey / V=shows / O=that 節 (接続詞 that が省略)
  O 内は `A for X, but B for Y` の対比。needing ~ は tasks を後置修飾する現在分詞。
  matching ~ = 分詞構文で「その事実が何と噛み合うか」を添える。

## 📍 本文の根拠
図(Source B)より、「Deep reading」は Paper 72%、「Memorizing」は Paper 65% で紙が多数。
「Quick search」は E-book 80%、「Carrying many books」は E-book 85% で電子が多数。
集中・記憶は紙、検索・携帯は電子という並びは、Aoi の「it depends on what you are doing」と、
Source A の「For tasks like quick searching or skimming, digital texts can even be more efficient.」に一致する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because most students chose e-books for carrying many books, e-books must also be better for deep reading.」… 携帯性の数値から深い読みへ結論を広げている。図では Deep reading は Paper 72% で、むしろ逆の結果。
- 「Since 72% preferred paper for deep reading, no student finds e-books useful for any purpose.」… 同じ図で Quick search 80%、Carrying many books 85% が電子を選んでいる。「どの用途でも役に立たない」は成り立たない。
- 「The high e-book figure for quick search proves that paper books make searching impossible.」… 図が示すのは選好の割合であって可否ではない。多くが電子を選んだことから「紙では検索できない」は導けない。

question_data.passage:
For your school newspaper, you are writing an essay about the question, "Should students wear school uniforms, or should they be allowed to wear their own clothes?" To prepare, you collected opinions from four classmates and found two sources of information.

Mika: I think uniforms are a good idea, but only because they make mornings easier. When I had to choose my own clothes for a school trip last year, I spent twenty minutes deciding and was almost late. With a uniform, I never have to think about what to wear. Still, I admit the design of our uniform is uncomfortable in summer, so I would not be sad if the school let us wear cooler clothes on very hot days. The point for me is saving time and trouble, not looking the same as everyone else.

Daniel: Honestly, I am against uniforms. Clothes are one of the few ways students can show who they are, and a uniform takes that freedom away. When everyone wears the same thing, we lose a chance to express our personalities and respect each other's differences. Some people say uniforms stop bullying, but I have seen students teased about other things, like their bags or shoes. A piece of clothing will not solve that problem. I would rather we learn to accept different styles than hide them.

Saki: I support uniforms, mainly for a reason people often forget: cost. Buying fashionable clothes every season is expensive, and not every family can afford it. If we wore our own clothes, students from richer families might show off, and others could feel left out or embarrassed. A uniform hides those differences, so no one is judged by how much money their family has. To me, fairness between students matters more than personal style.

Ren: I am somewhere in the middle. I do not think the school should force everyone into the exact same outfit, but total freedom could cause problems too. My idea is a set of rules instead, such as choosing from a few approved colors. That way students keep some choice while the school keeps order. What bothers me about strict uniforms is not the clothing itself but being told there is only one correct way to look.

Source A:
Researchers who study school clothing policies point out that the effects of uniforms are often misunderstood. Uniforms do not directly improve test scores; what matters is the sense of belonging and routine they can create. In schools where uniforms work well, students report feeling part of a community and waste less time on appearance, leaving more energy for learning. However, the same studies warn that uniforms alone cannot stop social problems. Bullying and exclusion are driven by differences in money, popularity, and behavior, and these continue even when clothing is identical. The clearest benefit, experts agree, is practical: a shared rule removes daily decisions and small status competitions over fashion, but only if the rule is applied fairly to everyone.

Source B (the graph below): A national group surveyed high school students and asked them to name the single most important reason they preferred uniforms or preferred their own clothes. The results are shown for four reasons.

questions.stem: What do Daniel and Ren have in common in their opinions?
choices: Both believe uniforms successfully prevent bullying at school.
Both want the school to remove all clothing rules completely.
Both think saving money is the strongest reason for uniforms.
Both dislike being forced into only one accepted way of looking.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Both dislike being forced into only one accepted way of looking.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 共通点は「賛成しているもの」だけでなく「**反対しているもの**」でも揃う。
  二人が何を嫌っているかを言い換えて重ねる。
- `be forced into ~` = 「〜へ押し込まれる」。`only one correct way` の **only** が争点。
- `not A but B` = 「AではなくB」。反発の対象が B 側に置かれる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Ren の中心文:
`[What bothers me about strict uniforms] is [not the clothing itself] but [being told [there is only one correct way to look]].`
  S=What bothers me about strict uniforms (関係代名詞 what 節が主語)
  V=is / C=not the clothing itself but being told ~ (not A but B・B は動名詞の受動)
→ 服そのものではなく「唯一の正解を言い渡されること」に反発している、と明示している。
  これが Daniel の「a uniform takes that freedom away」と同じ争点。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段 Daniel「Clothes are one of the few ways students can show who they are, and a uniform takes that freedom away.」
第4段 Ren「What bothers me about strict uniforms is not the clothing itself but being told there is only one correct way to look.」
二人とも、見た目を一つに強制されることへの反発で一致する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Both believe uniforms successfully prevent bullying at school.」… Daniel は「A piece of clothing will not solve that problem.」といじめ防止効果を否定している。Ren もいじめには触れていない。
- 「Both want the school to remove all clothing rules completely.」… Ren は「total freedom could cause problems too」と述べ、「a few approved colors」という規則を提案している。規則の全廃は求めていない。
- 「Both think saving money is the strongest reason for uniforms.」… 費用を最も重い理由に挙げるのは Saki。Daniel も Ren も費用には触れていない。

questions.stem: Whose opinion best agrees with the explanation given in Source A?
choices: Mika, because Source A says the clearest benefit of uniforms is practical.
Saki, because Source A says uniforms end all unfairness between families.
Daniel, because Source A says clothing freedom raises test scores.
Ren, because Source A recommends a few approved colors for students.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Mika, because Source A says the clearest benefit of uniforms is practical.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「誰が資料と合うか」型は、選択肢の **because 以下まで含めて**正誤を決める。
  人が合っていても理由が資料の記述と違えば誤り。
- `practical` = 「実用的」。資料が利点を **practical** と限定していることが手がかり。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Source A の結論文:
`[The clearest benefit], experts agree, is [practical]: [a shared rule] removes [daily decisions and small status competitions over fashion], but only if [the rule] is applied [fairly] [to everyone].`
  S=The clearest benefit / V=is / C=practical / 挿入=experts agree
  コロン以降が practical の中身: S=a shared rule / V=removes / O=daily decisions and small status competitions
  but only if ~ = 条件つきの限定 (公平に適用される場合に限る)

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A「The clearest benefit, experts agree, is practical: a shared rule removes daily decisions and small status competitions over fashion, but only if the rule is applied fairly to everyone.」
Mika はまさにこの実用面を理由に挙げており、「With a uniform, I never have to think about what to wear.」
「The point for me is saving time and trouble, not looking the same as everyone else.」と述べている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Saki, because Source A says uniforms end all unfairness between families.」… Source A は「uniforms alone cannot stop social problems」「these continue even when clothing is identical」と述べ、不公平が解消されるとは書いていない。
- 「Daniel, because Source A says clothing freedom raises test scores.」… Source A は「Uniforms do not directly improve test scores」と述べるだけで、服装の自由が成績を上げるとは書いていない。
- 「Ren, because Source A recommends a few approved colors for students.」… 「a few approved colors」は Ren 自身の提案であって、Source A の記述ではない。

questions.stem: What can be concluded from Source A?
choices: Making all students wear identical clothing removes social problems such as bullying.
Uniforms help mainly by reducing daily choices, not by directly raising academic results.
Schools with uniforms always have higher test scores than schools without them.
The biggest advantage of uniforms is that they make students express themselves freely.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Uniforms help mainly by reducing daily choices, not by directly raising academic results.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 資料の結論は「**何をしないか**」と「**何をするか**」を両方おさえると決まる。
  ここでは「成績を直接上げるのではない」＋「日々の決定を取り除く」。
- `not by ~ing` は**手段の否定**。何によって効くのかを限定する型。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Source A 冒頭:
`[Uniforms] do not directly improve [test scores]; [what matters] is [the sense of belonging and routine [they can create]].`
  S=Uniforms / V=do not improve / O=test scores / M=directly
  セミコロン以降: S=what matters (関係代名詞 what 節) / V=is
  C=the sense of belonging and routine they can create (they can create は routine を後置修飾)

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A「Uniforms do not directly improve test scores; what matters is the sense of belonging and routine they can create.」
と「The clearest benefit, experts agree, is practical: a shared rule removes daily decisions and small status competitions over fashion」。
この 2 文を合わせると、効き目は学力そのものではなく日々の選択を減らす点にあると結論できる。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Making all students wear identical clothing removes social problems such as bullying.」… 「Bullying and exclusion are driven by differences in money, popularity, and behavior, and these continue even when clothing is identical.」と正面から矛盾する。
- 「Schools with uniforms always have higher test scores than schools without them.」… 「Uniforms do not directly improve test scores」と矛盾する。always higher とは書かれていない。
- 「The biggest advantage of uniforms is that they make students express themselves freely.」… 制服は服装による自己表現をむしろ減らす側で、Source A も自己表現を利点として挙げていない。

questions.stem: Source B shows the survey results. Which statement is best supported when the data is combined with the classmates' opinions?
choices: Because 'Stopping bullying' got the lowest share, the survey proves uniforms cause bullying.
Most students chose 'Self-expression,' so the data clearly supports Saki's view about cost.
The reason Mika emphasizes was chosen by more students than any other single reason.
Since 'Lower cost' and 'Self-expression' together pass 50%, students mainly reject uniforms.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The reason Mika emphasizes was chosen by more students than any other single reason.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `more ... than any other + 単数名詞` = 「他のどれよりも〜」で、事実上の最上級。
- 図と意見を結ぶ設問では、まず**その人が挙げた理由がグラフのどの項目か**を特定する。
  ここでは Mika の「時間と手間の節約」＝ Saving time。

## 🔬 文構造分析
正答の選択肢:
`[The reason [Mika emphasizes]] was chosen [by more students] [than any other single reason].`
  S=The reason Mika emphasizes (目的格の関係代名詞が省略され、Mika emphasizes が the reason を修飾)
  V=was chosen (受動態) / M=by more students than any other single reason
→ 「Mika が強調する理由」を主語にまとめてから、最上級相当の比較で受ける形。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mika が最重視するのは「The point for me is saving time and trouble, not looking the same as everyone else.」。
図(Source B)の「Saving time」は 34% で、Self-expression 29%、Lower cost 25%、Stopping bullying 12% の
いずれよりも多い。つまり Mika の挙げた理由が単独で最多。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because 'Stopping bullying' got the lowest share, the survey proves uniforms cause bullying.」… 図は「最も重要と考える理由」の割合であって、いじめの原因を示すものではない。最小値から因果を導いている。
- 「Most students chose 'Self-expression,' so the data clearly supports Saki's view about cost.」… Self-expression は 29% で最多ではない (Saving time が 34%)。しかも自己表現は制服に反対する側の理由で、費用を挙げる Saki の主張とは結びつかない。
- 「Since 'Lower cost' and 'Self-expression' together pass 50%, students mainly reject uniforms.」… Lower cost (25%) は制服を支持する理由、Self-expression (29%) は制服に反対する理由で向きが逆。足し合わせて「制服を拒否」とは読めない。

question_data.passage:
In your English class, you are writing an essay on the question: "As we plan for the future of education, should schools focus more on online classes or on in-person classes?" You collected opinions from four classmates and two sources to support your writing.

Hana: I really believe online classes should be at the center of future learning. When my family moved last year, I could keep attending my old school's lessons from home without losing any time. Online classes also let students rewatch recorded lessons until they truly understand, and shy students who never speak in a classroom often ask questions through chat. For students in small towns far from good schools, the internet is the only way to reach skilled teachers. We should not throw away a tool that opens doors for so many people.

Daniel: I understand the appeal, but I think in-person classes must remain the heart of school. Learning is not only about information; it is about working with others, reading faces, and building friendships. At home, many of my classmates leave the camera off and quietly do other things. Teachers cannot notice when a student is confused or upset through a screen. The skills we need for work and life, like teamwork and patience, grow best when real people share the same room.

Aisha: I don't think we must choose only one. A "blended" approach makes the most sense to me. Routine lessons, such as watching a science video or practicing grammar, work well online and save travel time. But discussions, science experiments, and group projects belong in the classroom. If schools mix the two wisely, students enjoy both freedom and human connection. The real question is not online or in-person, but which subjects and activities suit each style.

Kenji: Honestly, I worry that we are rushing into online learning too quickly. Not every family has a fast internet connection or a quiet space to study, so some students are left behind. Staring at a screen for hours also tires the eyes and makes it hard to focus. I am not against technology, but until these problems are solved fairly for everyone, schools should keep in-person lessons as the safe and equal foundation for all students.

Source A
Researchers who study education warn that the format of a class matters less than how carefully it is designed. A well-planned online lesson with clear goals, regular feedback, and chances for students to interact can match or even beat a poorly run classroom lesson. However, studies also find that younger learners and those who struggle to manage their own time tend to fall behind when left alone in front of a screen. These students benefit most from the structure and personal attention of a classroom. Experts therefore advise schools not to ask "which format is better?" but rather "which format fits this lesson, this subject, and these particular students?" The goal, they argue, should be the right tool for each purpose, not one tool for everything.

Source B
A national group surveyed high school students who had experienced both online and in-person classes. Students were asked which format they felt was better for four different purposes. The graph below shows the percentage of students who chose "online" for each purpose. (Source B is shown in the graph below.)

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses Aisha's main point?
choices: Online classes should gradually replace in-person classes in every subject.
Online learning should be avoided until internet access becomes equal for all.
Schools should match each subject or activity to the format that suits it best.
In-person classes are the only way to build real friendships at school.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Schools should match each subject or activity to the format that suits it best.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `blended` = 「混ぜた」。二者択一を否定する意見は、必ず「では**何で振り分けるか**」の
  基準を示す。そこが主張の核になる。
- `belong in ~` = 「〜にこそ属する」。そこが本来の居場所だ、という強い言い方。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Aisha の結論文:
`[The real question] is [not online or in-person], but [which subjects and activities suit each style].`
  S=The real question / V=is
  C=not A but B (B に疑問詞節 which subjects and activities suit each style が入る)
→ 二択そのものを退けて、問いを「どれがどちらに向くか」へ立て直している。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段 Aisha。「A "blended" approach makes the most sense to me.」と立場を示し、
「Routine lessons, such as watching a science video or practicing grammar, work well online and save travel time. But discussions, science experiments, and group projects belong in the classroom.」
と振り分けを例示したうえで、「The real question is not online or in-person, but which subjects and activities suit each style.」と結ぶ。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Online classes should gradually replace in-person classes in every subject.」… Aisha は「discussions, science experiments, and group projects belong in the classroom」と教室に残すものを明示している。全科目のオンライン化とは逆。
- 「Online learning should be avoided until internet access becomes equal for all.」… 通信環境の格差を理由に慎重を求めるのは Kenji の立場。Aisha は環境格差には触れていない。
- 「In-person classes are the only way to build real friendships at school.」… 対面でしか育たないものを強調するのは Daniel。Aisha は両方を使い分けると述べている。

questions.stem: What is one point on which Hana and Kenji disagree?
choices: Whether the internet helps students who live far from good schools or instead leaves some students behind.
Whether students should ever be allowed to rewatch recorded lessons.
Whether teamwork and patience can be learned at school.
Whether teachers can notice a confused student through a screen.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Whether the internet helps students who live far from good schools or instead leaves some students behind.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「意見が食い違う点」を問う設問は、**同じ対象について逆の評価**をしている箇所を探す。
  ここでは「インターネット」という同じ対象が、片方では救いの手段、片方では格差の原因。
- `Not every ~` は**部分否定**で「すべてが〜なわけではない」。
- `leave ~ behind` = 「置き去りにする」。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Hana: `[For students in small towns far from good schools], [the internet] is [the only way [to reach skilled teachers]].`
  M=For students in small towns far from good schools / S=the internet / V=is
  C=the only way to reach skilled teachers (to 不定詞が way を修飾)
Kenji: `[Not every family] has [a fast internet connection or a quiet space to study], so [some students] are left behind.`
  S=Not every family (部分否定) / V=has / O=a fast internet connection or a quiet space to study
  so 節: S=some students / V=are left behind (受動態)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段 Hana「For students in small towns far from good schools, the internet is the only way to reach skilled teachers.」
第4段 Kenji「Not every family has a fast internet connection or a quiet space to study, so some students are left behind.」
同じインターネットを、届かない生徒に届く手段と見るか、届かない生徒を置き去りにする原因と見るかで割れている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Whether students should ever be allowed to rewatch recorded lessons.」… 録画の見返しは Hana が利点として挙げるだけで、Kenji は触れていない。対立点になっていない。
- 「Whether teamwork and patience can be learned at school.」… teamwork と patience を挙げるのは Daniel。Hana と Kenji の対立点ではない。
- 「Whether teachers can notice a confused student through a screen.」… 画面越しでは気づけないと述べるのは Daniel。Hana と Kenji の対立点ではない。

questions.stem: Whose opinion is most consistent with the advice given in Source A?
choices: Hana, because Source A says online classes are always better than classroom lessons.
Aisha, because Source A says schools should choose the format that fits each lesson and student.
Kenji, because Source A says online learning should wait until access is equal.
Daniel, because Source A says in-person classes should remain the heart of school.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Aisha, because Source A says schools should choose the format that fits each lesson and student.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 資料が「**問いの立て方そのものを変えよ**」と言っている場合、その新しい問いに沿って
  考えている人が正解になる。
- `advise A not to ask X but rather Y` = 「AにXではなくむしろYを問うよう勧める」。
  not A but rather B の骨格を外さないこと。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Experts] therefore advise [schools] [not to ask "which format is better?" but rather "which format fits this lesson, this subject, and these particular students?"].`
  S=Experts / V=advise / O=schools
  C=不定詞句 (目的格補語)。中身は not to ask A but rather B の対比。
→ 退けられているのは「どちらが優れるか」という問いそのもの。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A「Experts therefore advise schools not to ask "which format is better?" but rather "which format fits this lesson, this subject, and these particular students?"」
「The goal, they argue, should be the right tool for each purpose, not one tool for everything.」
これは Aisha の「The real question is not online or in-person, but which subjects and activities suit each style.」と同じ問いの立て方。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Hana, because Source A says online classes are always better than classroom lessons.」… Source A は「A well-planned online lesson with clear goals, regular feedback, and chances for students to interact can match or even beat a poorly run classroom lesson.」と条件つきで述べるだけで、常に優るとは書いていない。
- 「Kenji, because Source A says online learning should wait until access is equal.」… Source A に「通信環境が公平になるまで待て」という記述は無い。Kenji 自身の主張であって資料の裏づけではない。
- 「Daniel, because Source A says in-person classes should remain the heart of school.」… Source A は形式の優劣ではなく設計の質と生徒の特性で判断せよと述べており、対面を中心に据えよとは言っていない。

questions.stem: Which conclusion can best be drawn from Source A?
choices: Classroom lessons are always superior to online lessons regardless of planning.
Online lessons are always superior as long as they include videos and chat.
Younger students learn just as well online as older students do.
The quality of a lesson's design matters more than whether it is online or in-person, but some students still need a classroom's structure.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The quality of a lesson's design matters more than whether it is online or in-person, but some students still need a classroom's structure.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 資料が**一般論と例外**を両方述べているときは、片方だけの選択肢は必ず落ちる。
  「ただし〜な生徒は別」という但し書きまで含めた選択肢を選ぶ。
- `matters less than ~` = 「〜ほどには重要でない」。`tend to ~` = 「〜しがち」で断定を避ける形。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Researchers [who study education]] warn [that [the format of a class] matters [less than how carefully it is designed]].`
  S=Researchers who study education / V=warn / O=that 節
  that 節内: S=the format of a class / V=matters / M=less than how carefully it is designed
  (比較の対象に疑問詞節が入り、「形式」対「設計の丁寧さ」を天秤にかけている)

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A は「the format of a class matters less than how carefully it is designed」で一般論を置き、
続けて「However, studies also find that younger learners and those who struggle to manage their own time tend to fall behind when left alone in front of a screen. These students benefit most from the structure and personal attention of a classroom.」
と例外を述べる。両方を含む結論だけが本文全体と整合する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Classroom lessons are always superior to online lessons regardless of planning.」… 「the format of a class matters less than how carefully it is designed」と矛盾する。設計を無視して形式だけで優劣は決まらない。
- 「Online lessons are always superior as long as they include videos and chat.」… Source A が挙げる条件は「clear goals, regular feedback, and chances for students to interact」。動画とチャットさえあれば常に優るとは書いていない。
- 「Younger students learn just as well online as older students do.」… 「younger learners and those who struggle to manage their own time tend to fall behind when left alone in front of a screen」と正反対。

questions.stem: Which statement is best supported by combining Source B with the classmates' opinions?
choices: Because most students preferred online for making friends, Daniel's worry about losing friendships is unfounded.
Because only 14% preferred online for making friends, online classes have no real value for any purpose.
Since 78% preferred online for reviewing lessons, schools should move all subjects online as Hana wishes.
Students tended to prefer online for individual tasks like reviewing and saving time, but in-person for social tasks like discussion and friendship, which supports Aisha's blended approach.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Students tended to prefer online for individual tasks like reviewing and saving time, but in-person for social tasks like discussion and friendship, which supports Aisha's blended approach.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 用途別のグラフは「**一人でする作業**」と「**人と関わる作業**」で線を引くと読みやすい。
  その線引き自体が、用途で使い分けよという主張の裏づけになる。
- `which` の非制限用法は、**直前の内容全体**を受けて「そのことが〜」とつなぐ。

## 🔬 文構造分析
正答の選択肢:
`[Students] tended to prefer [online] [for individual tasks like reviewing and saving time], but [in-person] [for social tasks like discussion and friendship], [which supports Aisha's blended approach].`
  S=Students / V=tended to prefer / O=online ... but in-person ...(目的語が対比で 2 つ)
  which ~ = 関係代名詞の非制限用法。前の内容全体を受ける。

## 📍 本文の根拠
図(Source B)より、オンラインを選んだ割合は「Reviewing lessons at own pace」78%、
「Saving travel time」71% と高く、「Group discussion」22%、「Making friends」14% と低い。
一人でする作業と人と関わる作業のあいだに線が引ける。これは Aisha の
「The real question is not online or in-person, but which subjects and activities suit each style.」を裏づける。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because most students preferred online for making friends, Daniel's worry about losing friendships is unfounded.」… 図では「Making friends」でオンラインを選んだのは 14% と 4 項目中最も低い。前提が図と逆になっている。
- 「Because only 14% preferred online for making friends, online classes have no real value for any purpose.」… 同じ図で「Reviewing lessons at own pace」78%、「Saving travel time」71% と高い用途がある。ひとつの低い数値から全否定へ飛躍している。
- 「Since 78% preferred online for reviewing lessons, schools should move all subjects online as Hana wishes.」… 復習の数値だけを根拠に全科目へ広げている。討論 22%、友達づくり 14% という低い用途を無視した過度の一般化。

question_data.passage:
You are writing an essay for your English class on the question, "Is promoting tourism in our local area good for the people who live there?" To prepare, you collected opinions from four classmates and two sources of information.

[Opinions from classmates]

Mei: I think bringing more tourists to our town is clearly a good thing. Before the new train line opened, half the shops near the station were empty, and many of my friends' parents lost their jobs. Now small restaurants, guesthouses, and craft shops are busy again, and some young people who moved away have come back to work. Tourism gives our town money it badly needs, and that money pays for schools and roads. To me, a town with visitors is a living town, not a dying one.

Daniel: I understand the money side, but I am against pushing tourism so hard. On weekends I can no longer use my own neighborhood properly. The buses are full of visitors, the streets are noisy late at night, and it takes me twice as long to do simple shopping. We residents pay taxes here and live here every day, yet our daily lives are becoming harder so that strangers can enjoy themselves for a weekend. A town should serve the people who live in it first.

Sophie: Whether tourism helps or hurts depends entirely on how the town manages it. If thousands of people arrive with no rules, we get crowding, rising prices, and damage. But if the town sets limits, charges visitors a small fee, and uses that fee to fix problems, tourism can be good for everyone. The benefits and the problems usually appear together, so the real question is not "tourism: yes or no?" but "how do we control it well?"

Kenji: My worry is the natural environment. Our coast and forest are the reason tourists come, but more visitors means more trash, more cars, and more damage to the very places we love. Money is useful, but once a beautiful river or beach is ruined, no amount of money brings it back. If we protect nature first, tourism can continue for many years. If we ignore it, we sell our future for a quick profit.

Source A
Researchers who study "sustainable tourism" point out that the choice is rarely between welcoming all visitors and refusing them. In many towns, uncontrolled tourism does raise incomes at first, but crowding, higher prices, and environmental damage soon push local residents to oppose it. The towns that keep both their economy and their residents' goodwill tend to be the ones that manage visitor numbers actively. Common tools include daily limits on entry to popular sites, a small visitor fee, and spending that fee on local transport, cleaning, and repairs. Studies report that when such measures are introduced, both tourism income and resident satisfaction can rise together, because the benefits stay while the worst problems are reduced.

Source B
A town office surveyed local residents and asked which effects of recent tourism they had personally experienced. The results are shown in the graph below.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main point of Mei's opinion?
choices: Tourism brings income that revives local business and keeps the town alive.
Tourists should be welcomed only if the town first sets clear rules.
The natural environment matters more than the money tourism brings.
Residents' daily lives become harder when too many tourists arrive.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Tourism brings income that revives local business and keeps the town alive.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 要旨を問う設問は、その人が**繰り返し戻ってくる論点**を探す。
  Mei は「お金 → 商売の復活 → 町が生きる」を一貫して語っている。
- `a living town, not a dying one` の one は town の代用。対比で締める常套句。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Tourism] gives [our town] [money [it badly needs]], and [that money] pays for [schools and roads].`
  S=Tourism / V=gives / O1=our town / O2=money it badly needs
  (it badly needs は money を修飾する関係詞節。目的格の関係代名詞が省略されている)
  等位節: S=that money / V=pays for / O=schools and roads
→ 「観光 → 町にお金 → 学校と道路」という一本の流れが、そのまま要旨。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段 Mei。「Now small restaurants, guesthouses, and craft shops are busy again, and some young people who moved away have come back to work.」
で商売と雇用の回復を挙げ、「Tourism gives our town money it badly needs, and that money pays for schools and roads.」
と続け、「To me, a town with visitors is a living town, not a dying one.」で締める。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Tourists should be welcomed only if the town first sets clear rules.」… ルールを先に定めることを条件に据えるのは Sophie の立場。Mei は条件を付けていない。
- 「The natural environment matters more than the money tourism brings.」… 自然環境を金銭より優先せよと述べるのは Kenji の立場。
- 「Residents' daily lives become harder when too many tourists arrive.」… 住民の日常が苦しくなると訴えるのは Daniel の立場。Mei はむしろ町が生き返ったと述べている。

questions.stem: What do Sophie and Kenji have in common in how they think about tourism?
choices: Both believe tourism should be stopped completely in their town.
Both argue that tourism is acceptable only if its harmful effects are controlled or prevented.
Both think tourism mainly harms residents' daily shopping and transport.
Both claim that the economic benefits of tourism are not real.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Both argue that tourism is acceptable only if its harmful effects are controlled or prevented.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 共通点は「**条件つきの容認**」で揃うことがある。まず二人とも全否定していないことを確認し、
  次に「何が満たされれば認めるか」を並べる。
- `only if ~` = 「〜の場合に限り」。条件が満たされないと成り立たないことを示す。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Sophie: `[But if the town sets limits, charges visitors a small fee, and uses that fee to fix problems], [tourism] can be [good for everyone].`
  M(条件節)=if 節。sets / charges / uses の 3 動詞が並列
  S=tourism / V=can be / C=good for everyone
Kenji: `[If we protect nature first], [tourism] can continue [for many years].`
  M(条件節)=If we protect nature first / S=tourism / V=can continue
→ どちらも「if 節 + tourism can ~」という同じ骨格。条件が付く点で一致している。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段 Sophie「But if the town sets limits, charges visitors a small fee, and uses that fee to fix problems, tourism can be good for everyone.」
第4段 Kenji「If we protect nature first, tourism can continue for many years.」
二人とも観光を全否定せず、害を抑える条件のもとでのみ認めている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Both believe tourism should be stopped completely in their town.」… 二人とも「tourism can be good for everyone」「tourism can continue for many years」と、条件つきなら続けられると述べている。全面禁止は主張していない。
- 「Both think tourism mainly harms residents' daily shopping and transport.」… 買い物や交通の不便を中心に訴えるのは Daniel。Sophie は管理の仕方、Kenji は自然環境を論点にしている。
- 「Both claim that the economic benefits of tourism are not real.」… Kenji は「Money is useful」と経済的利益を認めている。Sophie も利益と問題が同時に現れると述べており、利益を否定していない。

questions.stem: Whose opinion is most directly supported by the information in Source A?
choices: Daniel, because Source A says residents should always come before visitors.
Mei, because Source A says tourism income always keeps rising.
Sophie, because Source A says actively managing visitor numbers lets income and resident satisfaction rise together.
Kenji, because Source A says nature can never be repaired once damaged.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Sophie, because Source A says actively managing visitor numbers lets income and resident satisfaction rise together.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「誰が資料に支持されるか」型は、資料の**因果の結論**をそのまま述べている人を選ぶ。
- 選択肢の because 以下が**資料に実際に書かれているか**を必ず確かめる。
  もっともらしいが資料に無い理由が並ぶのが、この形式の定石。

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Studies] report [that [when such measures are introduced], [both tourism income and resident satisfaction] can rise [together], because [the benefits] stay [while the worst problems are reduced]].`
  S=Studies / V=report / O=that 節
  that 節内: M(時の節)=when such measures are introduced
            S=both tourism income and resident satisfaction / V=can rise / M=together
  because 節がその理由。while は対比ではなく「〜する一方で」の同時進行。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A「The towns that keep both their economy and their residents' goodwill tend to be the ones that manage visitor numbers actively.」
「Studies report that when such measures are introduced, both tourism income and resident satisfaction can rise together, because the benefits stay while the worst problems are reduced.」
これは Sophie の「Whether tourism helps or hurts depends entirely on how the town manages it.」と直接一致する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Daniel, because Source A says residents should always come before visitors.」… Source A に「住民を常に訪問者より優先せよ」という記述は無い。資料が論じているのは管理の仕方。
- 「Mei, because Source A says tourism income always keeps rising.」… Source A は「uncontrolled tourism does raise incomes at first, but ...」と、収入が上がるのは最初だけだと明示している。always keeps rising とは書いていない。
- 「Kenji, because Source A says nature can never be repaired once damaged.」… 「once a beautiful river or beach is ruined, no amount of money brings it back」は Kenji 自身の言葉であって、Source A の記述ではない。

questions.stem: Which conclusion can best be drawn from Source A?
choices: Refusing all tourists is the only way to protect residents' daily lives.
Tourism income and resident satisfaction can never rise at the same time.
Visitor fees should be returned to tourists rather than spent in the town.
How a town manages tourism, rather than tourism itself, decides whether residents end up supporting or opposing it.
questions.explanation:
正解は「How a town manages tourism, rather than tourism itself, decides whether residents end up supporting or opposing it.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `A rather than B` = 「BではなくA」で**前が主役**。
- 資料が「無秩序なら反発 / 管理すれば両立」と、**同じ観光でも結果が割れる**ことを示していれば、
  分岐点は観光そのものではなく管理の仕方だと結論できる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
正答の選択肢:
`[How a town manages tourism], rather than [tourism itself], decides [whether residents end up supporting or opposing it].`
  S=How a town manages tourism (疑問詞節が主語)
  挿入=rather than tourism itself (主語の対比を割り込ませる)
  V=decides / O=whether 節 (支持に回るか反対に回るか)

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A は「In many towns, uncontrolled tourism does raise incomes at first, but crowding, higher prices, and environmental damage soon push local residents to oppose it.」
で無秩序な場合を述べ、「The towns that keep both their economy and their residents' goodwill tend to be the ones that manage visitor numbers actively.」
で管理した場合を述べる。同じ観光でも管理の有無で結果が分かれている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Refusing all tourists is the only way to protect residents' daily lives.」… 冒頭で「the choice is rarely between welcoming all visitors and refusing them」と、その二択自体を退けている。
- 「Tourism income and resident satisfaction can never rise at the same time.」… 「both tourism income and resident satisfaction can rise together」と正面から矛盾する。
- 「Visitor fees should be returned to tourists rather than spent in the town.」… 「spending that fee on local transport, cleaning, and repairs」と、料金を地域に使うことが挙げられている。訪問者への返金は書かれていない。

questions.stem: Which statement is best supported when Source B is read together with the classmates' opinions?
choices: Source B shows that jobs and crowding were both reported by large shares of residents, supporting Sophie's view that benefits and problems tend to appear together.
Source B shows crowding was reported by more residents than any other effect, confirming Daniel's view above all others.
Source B shows that almost no residents gained anything from tourism, proving Mei wrong.
Source B shows that better public facilities were the most common effect, supporting Kenji's environmental concern.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Source B shows that jobs and crowding were both reported by large shares of residents, supporting Sophie's view that benefits and problems tend to appear together.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「利益」と「問題」が**両方とも高い**グラフは、「どちらか一方」ではなく
  「**同時に起きる**」という主張を支える。
- 「最多はどれか」は必ず数値で確かめる。印象で決めると順位を取り違える。

## 🔬 文構造分析
正答の選択肢:
`[Source B] shows [that jobs and crowding were both reported [by large shares of residents]], [supporting Sophie's view [that benefits and problems tend to appear together]].`
  S=Source B / V=shows / O=that 節 (中は受動態 were reported。by ~ が動作主)
  supporting ~ = 分詞構文。末尾の that 節は view の同格。

## 📍 本文の根拠
図(Source B)より「More local jobs」64%、「Worse crowding/traffic」58% と、
利益と問題の両方が高い割合で報告されている。これは Sophie の
「The benefits and the problems usually appear together, so the real question is not "tourism: yes or no?" but "how do we control it well?"」
を最もよく支える。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Source B shows crowding was reported by more residents than any other effect, confirming Daniel's view above all others.」… 最も多く報告されたのは「More local jobs」64% で、混雑は 58%。「他のどの影響より多い」という前提が図と違う。
- 「Source B shows that almost no residents gained anything from tourism, proving Mei wrong.」… 64% が仕事の増加を報告している。「ほとんど誰も利益を得ていない」は図と矛盾する。
- 「Source B shows that better public facilities were the most common effect, supporting Kenji's environmental concern.」… 「Better public facilities」は 39% で 4 項目中最も低い。最多という前提が誤りで、公共施設は Kenji の自然環境の論点とも別。
